catalog.name: Oceans
catalog.description: Ocean and marine datasets from NASA Earth observation missions, including sea surface measurements and oceanographic parameters critical for understanding ocean dynamics and climate interactions.

info.name: Attribution
info.content: Data provided by NASA's Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS) and oceanographic missions. Contact: earthdata-support@nasa.gov

info.name: License
info.content: NASA data is generally available for public use. Please check individual dataset licenses and cite appropriately.

info.name: Coverage
info.content: Global ocean coverage with various temporal and spatial resolutions depending on the specific mission and instrument.

members.name: Sea Surface Dynamics
members.description: Ocean surface measurements including sea level anomalies and dynamic topography from satellite altimetry missions.

members.name: AVISO Absolute Dynamic Topography
members.description: Absolute Dynamic Topography (ADT) from AVISO satellite altimetry, representing sea surface height relative to the geoid and indicating ocean currents and circulation patterns.

info.name: Background
info.content: Absolute Dynamic Topography combines satellite altimetry measurements with a high-resolution mean sea surface and geoid model. ADT represents the sea surface height above the geoid and directly relates to ocean currents through geostrophic balance.

info.name: Measurement Principle
info.content: Satellite altimeters measure sea surface height by timing radar pulses. ADT is calculated by removing the geoid and adding the mean dynamic topography.

info.name: Spatial Resolution
info.content: 0.25° x 0.25° global grid, daily updates

info.name: Temporal Coverage
info.content: 1993 to present from multiple altimeter missions (TOPEX/Poseidon, Jason series, Sentinel-3, etc.)

info.name: Applications
info.content: Ocean current mapping, eddy detection, sea level rise studies, marine navigation, fisheries management, climate research

info.name: Data Provider
info.content: AVISO+ (Archiving, Validation and Interpretation of Satellite Oceanographic data)

info.name: Attribution
info.content: AVISO+ altimetry data produced by CLS/CNES. Distributed through NASA GIBS.

members.name: Sea Surface Temperature
members.description: Sea surface temperature measurements from various satellite missions, critical for understanding ocean-atmosphere interactions and climate patterns.

members.name: AIRS Sea Surface Temperature (Day)
members.description: Daytime surface air temperature measurements from the Atmospheric Infrared Sounder (AIRS) on NASA's Aqua satellite.

info.name: Background
info.content: Sea Surface Temperature (SST) is a key oceanographic parameter that influences weather patterns, marine ecosystems, and global climate. AIRS provides high-quality SST measurements using infrared radiation.

info.name: Measurement Technique
info.content: Infrared radiometry measuring thermal emission from the ocean surface skin layer (~10 μm depth)

info.name: Temporal Sampling
info.content: Daytime overpasses (~1:30 PM local time)

info.name: Spatial Resolution
info.content: 1° x 1° global grid

info.name: Accuracy
info.content: ±0.5K under clear sky conditions

info.name: Applications
info.content: Climate monitoring, weather forecasting, ocean-atmosphere interaction studies, marine ecosystem research

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA AIRS mission team, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory

members.name: AIRS Sea Surface Temperature (Night)
members.description: Nighttime surface air temperature measurements from AIRS, providing complementary data to daytime observations for diurnal cycle analysis.

info.name: Background
info.content: Nighttime SST measurements help understand diurnal temperature cycles in the ocean surface, which are important for air-sea interaction processes and marine ecosystem dynamics.

info.name: Temporal Sampling
info.content: Nighttime overpasses (~1:30 AM local time)

info.name: Diurnal Variation
info.content: Typically, nighttime SST is cooler than daytime due to surface cooling and reduced solar heating

info.name: Applications
info.content: Diurnal warming studies, air-sea heat flux calculations, marine boundary layer research

info.name: Attribution
info.content: NASA AIRS mission team, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory
